answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut is severe, but the 14-day expiry and 94% line utilization with no buffer make switching or adding a second source high-risk this cycle. Deferral (memory_c5 precedent) is not viable because the contract does not auto-renew; inaction equals loss of supply. The inherited record suggests that multi-year commitment leverage (memory_c6) combined with active benchmarking-based renegotiation (memory_c4) has previously recovered real margin without service disruption or migration cost. Negotiating renewal terms—extending term length for volume pricing while pressing on unit price and payment terms against current market rates—addresses the cost mandate directly while keeping the existing, stable supply relationship intact, which is the lowest-delivery-risk path given zero buffer on the line.
